# Page 5^page=5
OVERVIEW OF THE SCHEME A rebate is a partial refund of the cost of an item. It acts as an incentive to help sell the product.

# Page 6^page=6


# Page 7^page=7
• Objective - To make Indian textile exports globally price-competitive. It achieves this by reimbursing exporters for "hidden tax" or embedded state and central indirect taxes incurred during production ensuring a level playing field in the international market. Hidden taxes are indirect, often invisible charges built into the final price of goods and services, allowing governments to collect revenue without directly notifying consumers. Example - VAT on fuel used in transportation, Electricity duties, Mandi tax and municipal taxes, Stamp duty on export documents

# Page 8^page=8
TARGET TEXTILES Made-ups refers to finished, ready-to-use textile products made from woven or knitted fabrics that are not clothing (garments). These items are manufactured for home, hospitality, or industrial use, such as bedsheets, towels, curtains, table linens, and cushions

# Page 9^page=9
Zero-Rated Exports: It operates on the internationally accepted economic principle that "goods are exported and not domestic taxes". Freely Transferable

# Page 10^page=10
Feature RoSCTL RoDTEP Full Name Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products Launch Year Introduced earlier, in March 2019. Introduced later, in January 2021. Target Sector Only covers readymade garments, apparel, and textile made-ups (like bedsheets and curtains). Covers almost all other export sectors (agriculture, leather, electronics, machinery, raw yarn/fabric, etc.). Parent Ministry Notified by the Ministry of Textiles. Notified by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (specifically the DGFT). What it Replaced Replaced the older RoSL (Rebate of State Levies) scheme. Replaced the older MEIS (Merchandise Exports from India Scheme).

Q. Consider the following statements regarding the RoSCTL Scheme: 1. The scheme reimburses exporters for embedded state and central indirect taxes incurred during production. 2. It follows the principle that exported goods should carry domestic taxes to support government revenue. 3. The implementing agency of the scheme is the Department of Revenue under the Ministry of Finance. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
